text:
Nina (PMM): quick thread 12h triage to lock the battlecard + two launch posts for next week's webinar. Need defensible claims + routing tweaks for inbound demo requests.
Carlos (Growth): landing page copy needs two headline options to A/B. also want a short summary for paid social.
Asha (Field): reps asked for "one-line closes" and a 30s soundbite about outages/fallbacks. Keep it usable on calls.
Liam (Benchmark): high-level bench takeaways I can share:
- p99 tail latency control: observed < 250ms under 1k concurrent users in our harness
- cost delta: quantized model + batching shaved ~3x token spend in chat-heavy flows vs naive endpoints
- failover: automated model fallback kept throughput steady during a forced node loss test
Anita (Content): convert those into two public-safe lines and one sharp internal line per claim. Public = "customer-observed" phrasing.
Nina (PMM): suggested public lines:
- "Customer-observed p99 < 250ms under sustained load"
- "Measured token savings (up to 3x) with batching + quantization"
- "Single API across hosted, reserved, and private deployments"
Asha (Field): internal rep lines (1-liners):
- Latency: "Ask for our benchmark deck 1 slide: p99 < 250ms under sustained load"
- Cost: "We often see ~3x reduction for chat when batching + lightweight quantization are applied"
Riley (Sales Ops): routing rules proposal: if lead.activity contains "benchmark-slide" OR lead.company.size > 500 => route to AE; else standard SDR funnel. Add tag: benchmark_warm. Also record experiment param opener_variant (A or B).
Carlos (Growth): opener variants for ads/emails:
A) "How teams stabilize LLM latency and control per-token costs"
B) "Practical tradeoffs: Managed endpoints vs dedicated serving"
Carlos (Growth): run A on paid socials, B in nurture sequences. Tag ad clicks with opener=A.
Liam (Benchmark): deliverable: 3-slide benchmark summary + appendix with harness commands and synthetic distribution (due 3925001500).
Anita (Content): deliverable: 1) public blog-ready paragraph (customer-observed), 2) 1-page internal battlecard update with 6 quick rebuttals and 3 demo soundbites (due 3925001700).
Riley (Sales Ops): I'll push the SFDC tag + routing change. Also: add an automation to create task for AE when lead.tag includes benchmark_warm. Due 3925001850.
Nina (PMM): prioritize two rebuttals for the battlecard: cost and availability. Drafts?
Anita (Content): drafts below:
- "Why not just use a cloud provider endpoint?" -> "Cloud endpoints are easy to start with, but they don't give you deterministic capacity controls or the routing policies needed to protect tail latency in production. Redwood gives runbook-level controls and fallbacks you can rely on."
- "Can't we just own the model privately?" -> "Model ownership helps, but serving and runtime behavior determine cost and latency at scale. We provide the serving runtime, autoscaling policies, and KV/prefix caching to make that predictable."
Asha (Field): add one quick demo: show a short prompt where cloud endpoint stalls on multi-turn and Redwood returns stable latencies. We need a single anonymized example.
Liam (Benchmark): I'll add a slide: anonymized prompt -> response time timeline for both systems.
deploy-bot: assets uploaded to s3://redwood-assets/marketing/webinar-392500/bench-3slides.pdf at 3925001450
Nina (PMM): decision: Ads use opener A, nurture uses B. Field gets the sharper internal lines + "ask for benchmark deck" CTA. Routing rules implemented by Riley.
Carlos (Growth): tracking: create experiment key "webinar_opener_v3" and wire to analytics.
Riley (Sales Ops): noted. I'll also add a lead scoring boost for anyone who watches > 50% of webinar or clicks benchmark slide.
Anita (Content): keeping public claims conservative: swap exact numbers to "customer-observed" in public blog and keep concrete numbers in a gated benchmark deck.
Asha (Field): can we get a 1-paragraph playbook for SDRs on handling pricing pushback? 3 bullets max.
Anita (Content): will do in the battlecard.
Nina (PMM): ok team 12h check-in in this thread, deliverables due as noted. Move fast. :sparkles:
